gps.ghiChuNguon: The middle column is the distance the system sums from the denoised track, compared with the distance reported by the sitter app. A session is flagged only when the gap passes both thresholds: more than 0.3 km and more than 20% of the system figure. A noise point is a pair of consecutive points implying more than 40 km/h both inbound and outbound.

khieuNai.ghiChuEnum: A dispute file has three underlying states; the four shown here are derived from data: waiting on the sitter is a file still within the reply window, waiting for handling is a file past that window or under review, and resolved files split by whether money was refunded.
khieuNai.ghiChuGiuTien: Opening a dispute holds the money: the booking payout stays out of the sitter wallet until the file is resolved. The sitter replies exactly once within 48 hours; if that window passes in silence the file moves to the admin with an empty reply.

danhGia.ghiChuThieuModel: Each review holds a rating, a comment, up to 6 photos and one sitter reply. This screen is read only, an admin cannot take a review down yet. The owner has 7 days to review once the booking is completed and the sitter has 7 days to reply exactly once; after that the review is final.

moTa.SENT: Mark as transferred, the request now waits for the bank confirmation.
moTa.DONE: The bank confirmed, this withdrawal is complete.
moTa.REJECTED: Reject the request and return the balance to the sitter wallet.

taiChinh.ghiChuEnum: A withdrawal has four states: waiting for the transfer, transferred and waiting for the bank, complete, and rejected. The balance is deducted the moment the sitter creates the request rather than when the bank confirms, so a rejection must return it with a new ledger entry instead of deleting the old one. Minimum withdrawal is 50,000 VND, the transfer fee is currently 0.

dialogRaw.moTa: Read only. It is the only proof when reconciling with the gateway statement.
dialogRaw.chuaCoPayload: This record has no gateway response, the transaction never reached the gateway

thanhToan.ghiChuEnum: A payment has seven states: awaiting payment, held by the platform, released to the sitter wallet, refunding, refunded, declined by the gateway, and expired after the 10 minute hold. The Gateway column shows which mode created the record, the real gateway or the simulated mode toggled in System settings, and both follow the same flow. One booking can have several payments because a retry carries a new transaction reference, but only one payment may hold money at a time.

hoanTien.nguonNhan: The money goes back to {{bank}}, the exact source the owner paid from. The gateway never returns card numbers so none is shown here.
hoanTien.nguonNhanKhongRo: The money goes back to the source you paid from. This record has no bank code and the gateway never returns card numbers.

tieuDe.manual: Mark as refunded on the gateway portal

moTa.view: The transaction reference, the gateway reference and the gateway timestamp must all be intact for the refund to run.
moTa.manual: Use this when the gateway blocks automatic refunds: refund on the gateway portal first, then mark it here with the reference.

dialog.maGoiY: Enter the gateway refund reference for later reconciliation

hoanTien.ghiChuNguon: A refund reverses the original transaction, so the record must still carry the transaction reference, the gateway reference and the gateway timestamp; if any of the three is missing the refund cannot run. Owners have no wallet and never enter a bank account, the money goes back to the source they paid from. The gateway returns only the bank code and card type, never the card number. When the gateway blocks automatic refunds the admin refunds on the gateway portal and marks it here.
